summary.name: Tauri
summary.one_liner: Tauri is an open-source toolkit for building small, fast, secure cross-platform applications using any web frontend with a Rust backend.
keywords: build desktop apps with web technologies
use_cases: build a desktop app from an existing web frontend
ship one codebase to Linux, macOS, and Windows
create a mobile app for Android or iOS with web tech
make a small footprint desktop application
integrate native Swift or Kotlin code into an app
summary.what_it_does: Tauri lets you write the frontend in any web framework or in plain JavaScript, and the application logic in Rust. It targets Linux, macOS, Windows, Android and iOS from a single codebase. It uses the operating system's native web renderer rather than bundling one, which the page says can make an app as small as 600KB. The page also states that you can integrate deeply with the system using Swift and Kotlin. Security is presented as a top priority for the team, though the page gives no specifics.
notable: Uses the OS native web renderer, enabling apps as small as 600KB
Any frontend framework can be used without changing your stack
Application logic in Rust with Swift and Kotlin system integration
Single codebase for desktop and mobile
caveats: Page does not state specific pricing or license terms beyond a CC-BY / MIT footer note
Security claims are general with no concrete details on the page
Mobile support details beyond the listing are not elaborated on the page
